subject: Next steps: cost model & who signs (econ buyer / finance path)
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Lena Thompson <lena@fintechco.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: cost model & who signs (econ buyer / finance path)

Hi Lena — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can get a clean pricing path in front of your team:

- Summary of usage we heard: baseline ~1M tokens/month for production inference, bursty up to ~5M in peak periods (Q4 product ramp).
- Initial ask from your side: target unit economics and an order-of-magnitude monthly budget to fit into your FY26 planning. You mentioned wanting rough $/1M token guidance before taking anything to procurement.

To move forward, can you confirm two things for us: 1) who is the economic buyer that will sign off on pricing (name + title), and 2) who is the budget owner / finance contact that needs an SOW and PO (name + email)?

If it helps, attached is a simple pricing model I can pre-fill with your volumes (pricing-model.xlsx). If you can confirm the buyer and budget owner, I’ll put together two options: a usage-first quote (no commit) and a 12-month committed band with a discounted rate and reserved capacity terms.

Other quick questions: preferred invoice cadence (monthly/quarterly), and whether your procurement requires a PO number before execution or if DocuSign + invoice is acceptable.

Thanks — I’ll be standing by to fill the model.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
[Attachment: pricing-model.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
From: Lena Thompson <lena@fintechco.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Moretti <alex.moretti@fintechco.com>, Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>, Rachel Li <rachel.li@fintechco.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: cost model & who signs (econ buyer / finance path)

Hi Kim — great talk, thanks for the clear recap. Answers below: 

- Economic buyer: Alex Moretti, VP of AI (alex.moretti@fintechco.com) — Alex owns model spend and ROI approvals.
- Budget owner / finance: Rachel Li, Head of Product, is the day-to-day budget owner and will route to Finance for PO (rachel.li@fintechco.com). Procurement is copied (procurement@fintechco.com) for process.
- High-level budget range we’re comfortable sharing now: $20k–$40k / month initially (covers baseline + some burst); this is rough and dependent on the unit economics you propose.
- Invoice cadence preference: monthly invoices, Net30. Procurement indicated they prefer a PO when the amount is committed for a year; for short pilots they accept DocuSign + invoice.

If you can send the two quote options you mentioned (usage vs 12mo commit) and show the $/1M token figure in each, Alex and Rachel will be able to review. Happy to keep procurement in the loop.

Thanks,
Lena
Lena Thompson
Head of ML Ops, FintechCo
lena@fintechco.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Next steps: cost model & who signs (econ buyer / finance path) — pricing ask

Team — forwarding Lena’s confirmation (FintechCo). Key points: baseline ~1M / mo, burst to 5M, budget range $20–40k/mo, econ buyer = Alex Moretti, budget owner = Rachel Li, procurement prefers PO on multi-month/commits.

Attaching the pricing model with our recommended inputs. Can you advise:
- Recommended public list / starting band for usage (no commit) and a discounted committed 12-mo band to land inside their $20–40k/mo if possible. Show effective $ per 1M tokens for both.
- If we offer reserved capacity (pin 1M tokens/mo) what discount % can we give for a 12-mo commit? Any minimums we should be aware of?
- Procurement asks for SOW + SOC2. Do we have a stock SOW template and is it ok to send SOC2 report now?

I’ll draft the two quote options once you confirm numbers. I’d like to include a DocuSign path for pilots and a PO path for the commit.

Thanks,
—Kim
[Attachment: pricing-model.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 09:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Next steps: cost model & who signs (econ buyer / finance path) — pricing ask

Kim / team — recommended packaging for FintechCo: 

1) Usage-first (no commit) option
- Rate: $1,100 per 1M tokens (list), with tiered volume discounts after 3M/mo.
- Monthly billing, Net30. This keeps entry friction low for pilot.

2) 12‑month committed option (preferred)
- Commit: 1M tokens/month guaranteed for 12 months.
- Effective rate: $0.80 per 1M tokens on committed volume.
- Overages billed at $0.95 per 1M tokens.
- If they commit to 3M/month band we can do $0.70 per 1M for committed volume.

3) Commercial levers and onboarding credits
- Offer $15k in onboarding credits (applied over first 3 months) to offset ramp.
- Provide a short pilot via DocuSign (no PO) for up to 3 months; once they sign commit we switch to PO path.

Procurement path / docs
- Finance will require: SOW (we have a template), SOC2 report (we can share the current report), W9 and invoice. Procurement prefers a PO for any annual/committed spend. DocuSign is acceptable for short pilots.
- I’m attaching SOW stub. Once Kim finalizes volumes I’ll approve the quote for signature.

Next actions for Kim:
- Fill the pricing-model.xlsx with their monthly baseline and peak and send two numbered quote PDFs: (A) usage-first, (B) 12-mo commit with the reserved schedule.
- Copy Alex and Rachel plus procurement on the quote email; include SOW + SOC2 link.

I’ll sign off on the numbers once the model is filled.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Head of Commercial, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SOW-FintechCo-v1.pdf (SOW template)]
